text:
lei: Heads-up — seeing a bunch of training pods stuck Pending in us-west1-gpu-edge nodepool. Scheduler event: "0/12 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" but `kubectl top nodes` shows GPUs in use only ~30%.

maria: Can you paste `kubectl describe pod` for one of them?

lei: Paste below — shortened: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   3m    default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
```
Pod spec: requests: cpu 4, memory 32Gi, nvidia.com/gpu: 0.25 (we're using MIG-ish partitioning via device-plugin)

sam: Wait, are these pods requesting fractional GPUs? k8s device-plugins usually expose whole devices unless MIG is configured per-driver. Which device plugin are we using on these nodes?

lei: We use the vendor MIG plugin on A100s in that pool. But node labels differ: some nodes are labeled `gpu.redwood.com/mig=true`, others don't. I think CA (cluster-autoscaler) is scaling up non-MIG nodes.

jose: That matches a bug I saw — autoscaler chooses the cheapest instance type in the nodepool that fits CPU/mem but doesn't consider MIG capacity shape, so it brings up a single-A100 node that isn't partitioned, leaving fractional requests unschedulable.

infra-bot: [autoscaler] ScaleUp: nodepool us-west1-gpu-edge (request for 4 nodes) -> new instances: a100-1x, a40-1x (reason: cpu/mem fit) :thumbsdown:

maria: Two quick mitigations: 1) require pods to request whole MIG profiles (explicit `nvidia.com/mig.instances: "1g.5gb"`), or 2) change nodeSelector/taints so CA only picks MIG-enabled node types for that workload.

dave: Also consider adding a custom CA expander config so it prefers `gpu-mig` machine types when GPU resources are requested. CA currently uses lowest-cost policy.

sam: Another pattern: use topology-aware packing — set `podTopologySpread` or `nodeAffinity` to prefer packing to fully use GPUs on nodes (reduce fragmentation). Example snippet: 
```
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      nodeSelectorTerms:
      - matchExpressions:
        - key: gpu.redwood.com/mig
          operator: In
          values:
          - "true"
```

lei: Quick test: I added `nodeAffinity` to a Job and resubmitted — it scheduled immediately onto a MIG node. But this is a workaround, not a platform fix.

jose: Long-term: we should teach autoscaler about GPU shapes (MIG partitions) or maintain separate nodepools per GPU partitioning model with clear max/min and CA policies.

maria: Agreed. Action items: 1) add label `gpu.redwood.com/mig=true` to all MIG nodes and update CA expander preferences (sam), 2) tag workloads that need fractional GPUs and add admission webhook that enforces matching nodeSelector (lei), 3) short-term: cordon non-mig nodes in us-west1-gpu-edge to drain bad instances (dave).

lei: I'll cordon two suspicious nodes now: `kubectl cordon gpu-edge-17` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets`.

infra-bot: [node-manager] Node gpu-edge-17 cordoned by lei at 1770123488

maria: Also, let's file a follow-up to evaluate using CMA/Karpenter which has better instance-type selection based on pod-level resource shapes. CA is fine for general use but struggles with GPU fragmentation.

dave: Filing a short RFC in #eng-infra-rfcs with cost tradeoffs. For now we'll proceed with labeling + CA expander.

lei: Cool — will monitor and report back in 30m. :eyes:
